record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: In the single-server M/G/1 setting with unknown job sizes, can the known factor-5 guarantee for a simple policy relative to the optimal Gittins policy be improved, or can other simple policies be found that achieve comparably near-optimal mean response time?

evidence.quote: In [130], Scully et al. proved that a much simpler policy, related to SERPT, is within a factor 5 of optimal. It is an open problem whether that factor can be improved, or whether other simple policies with near-optimal mean response time exist.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an M/G/1 queue: jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$ to a single server, and each job has an i.i.d. size drawn from a distribution $S$ with finite mean, so that the load is $\rho = \lambda \mathbb{E}[S] < 1$. The scheduler may preempt jobs at any time but does not know the exact remaining size of a job; instead, for a job that has so far received service (age) $a$, the scheduler knows the conditional distribution of its remaining size given that it has been served for $a$ time units. A scheduling policy is a rule, based only on each job's age, deciding which job to serve at each instant. Let $\mathbb{E}[T^\pi]$ denote the steady-state mean response time (sojourn time) under policy $\pi$, and let $\mathrm{Gittins}$ denote the Gittins index policy, which is known to minimize $\mathbb{E}[T^\pi]$ in this setting.

Define the policy M-SERPT (monotonic shortest expected remaining processing time), which assigns to each job of age $a$ the rank
$$r(a) = \sup_{b \ge a} \, \mathbb{E}[S - a \mid S > a, \text{ remaining work after age } a \text{ is observed up to age } b],$$
or more simply a monotonized version of the expected-remaining-size function, and at all times serves the job of smallest rank. It is known that
$$\mathbb{E}[T^{\text{M-SERPT}}] \le 5 \, \mathbb{E}[T^{\text{Gittins}}]$$
for every job size distribution $S$ and every load $\rho < 1$.

(a) Can the constant $5$ in the above inequality be replaced by a smaller universal constant (and what is the optimal constant)?

(b) Does there exist another scheduling policy $\pi$, whose rank function is "simple" in the sense of being substantially less complex to compute than the Gittins index, such that $\mathbb{E}[T^\pi] \le C \, \mathbb{E}[T^{\text{Gittins}}]$ holds for a universal constant $C$, ideally with $C$ smaller than $5$?
artifact.status_search_result: The factor-5 bound was established by Scully, Harchol-Balter, and Scheller-Wolf (2019/2020) for M-SERPT versus Gittins. Subsequent work, including Scully's 2022 thesis and related papers, has refined the analysis (showing the ratio is at most 3 for load ρ ≤ 8/9) and noted that the worst observed ratio in examples is only about 2, but no published result improves the universal constant below 5 nor exhibits a different simple policy with a better universal approximation guarantee. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Simple Near-Optimal Scheduling for the M/G/1
status_evidence.snippet: M-SERPT is a 5-approximation for mean response time at all loads; ratio is at most 3 for ρ ≤ 8/9.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the factor-5 guarantee for M-SERPT relative to Gittins, which remains the best known universal bound.

status_evidence.title: A New Toolbox for Scheduling Theory (Scully thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: M-SERPT is the only non-Gittins scheduling policy known to have a constant-factor approximation ratio for mean response time.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2022 no other simple policy with a constant-factor near-optimal guarantee is known.
